branchWorkflows.name: Post-apocalyptic wasteland
branchWorkflows.procedure: Declare event, time since collapse, climate and current repair capacity. Build a thick intact facade/vehicle/shelter master, then separate event damage, long-term weathering and recent salvage. A 12 m street slice can have one intact anchor, one breached bay and one inhabited repair. Orient rubble/scorch to the event and dust to wind/shelter; later tracks cut through older deposits. Tie tarp corners to actual anchors and add supported patched panels. Use bleached sun-exposed paint, protected original color, material-specific corrosion and rough dust. Low hard light reveals damage depth, while neutral fill confirms interiors. If every substrate rusts, separate metal from concrete/glass/cloth masks. If habitation reads abandoned, add recent reachable tools, water access and repaired paths. Deliver chronology layers and clear-corridor/fog-off images; collapse art is not structural or survival-system validation.

branchWorkflows.name: Zombie city and human response
branchWorkflows.procedure: Build ordinary urban access first: storefront, stairs, windows and a rear escape. Add barricades from reachable salvage with meaningful braces, fastening and human movement clearances. Stage intact, freshly blocked and breached variants sharing pivots. Broken glass, dragged furniture and discarded supplies should describe direction of pressure and occupation, not random gore. Keep quiet safe-space signifiers distinct from environmental damage if supplied by the project. Separate old city weathering from fresh impacts, stains or makeshift repairs. Inspect entry/reverse views and crouched/standing proxies with effects off. A barricade that blocks all circulation needs redesigned placement, not silently shrunken actors. Clutter resembling pickups needs a distinct packaging/state grammar. Deliver door/window/barricade state sheet and assembly notes; zombie detection, AI routes and safe zones are not established by renders.

branchWorkflows.name: Alien invasion and unfamiliar damage
branchWorkflows.procedure: Define one coherent foreign fabrication/impact vocabulary and how it differs from local buildings. Construct an ordinary bay, a contact zone and a foreign insert or landing footprint with consistent connector scale. Impact deformation must have a direction, thickness and debris logic; an alien graft needs roots/anchors and service/growth paths. Keep human reference elements intact nearby so unfamiliar scale is legible. Use restrained foreign material response or a distinctive form hierarchy rather than making everything emissive. Render foreign layer off/on and a clean cross-section. If alien damage is indistinguishable from generic explosion rubble, revise characteristic cut/penetration/attachment shapes. If scale is unclear, add doors/vehicles with known size rather than labeling the object giant. Deliver source/contact/reaction layers and diagnostic close-ups; physical impact or fictional technology is unverified beyond the stated visual rule.

branchWorkflows.name: Post-human ecological succession
branchWorkflows.procedure: Set climate and elapsed time, then stage building failure, water paths and successive plant colonization. Begin with roof/drain breakage and soil pockets; place small growth there before large roots/trees. Substantial plants need plausible support volumes or explicit fantasy. Build an early/late pair from the same architecture with preserved source and cameras, changing masks/distribution rather than merely increasing a scatter count. Use moisture stains and protected versus exposed surfaces to connect vegetation to water. Show interiors and sheltered undersides, not only a green facade. If mature trees grow on unsupported glass, revise substrate/support. If lush growth contradicts a dry brief, adapt species/coverage and preserve the approved timeline. Deliver architecture/growth separately, succession masks and dry/wet contact views; these are authored visual states, not ecological simulation proof.

branchWorkflows.name: Dystopian control infrastructure
branchWorkflows.procedure: Use only the control/oppression story actually requested. Build barriers, observation positions, checkpoint hardware and permitted/service circulation around a normal civic block. Give cameras/gates real mounting, cable/power routes and maintenance access; separate active/inactive/breached states. Distinguish permanent authority construction from improvised public responses through assembly, scale and repair quality. Reserve graphic symbols/emission for selected control nodes. Frame both institutional wide symmetry and street-eye passage; inspect neutral lighting so intimidating grade does not replace actual spatial hierarchy. If all entrances look sealed but the brief needs habitation, add readable daily/service access. Deliver access-state sheet and hardware diagrams. Static sight cones or camera props do not prove surveillance, detection or authorization logic.

branchWorkflows.name: Utopian civic systems and requested uncanny contrast
branchWorkflows.procedure: Clean, functional civic design can be sincere. Build maintained transit/water/garden/repair systems, accessible entrances and human-scale public use before optional uncanny staging. Create a service-open variant showing how immaculate surfaces are cleaned and repaired. If the brief asks for an uneasy veneer, introduce controlled repetition, selectively absent use traces or a precise compositional anomaly rather than automatically adding propaganda. Use clean but varied roughness, realistic seams and restrained accents; avoid clipping white surfaces into featureless emission. Compare occupied/empty and neutral/atmospheric views. A sterile dollhouse needs contact, wear-at-use and service-scale correction. Deliver maintained/service/contrast states with exact intentional anomalies; no moral narrative or social outcome is inferred solely from the palette.

branchWorkflows.name: Underwater reef, open seabed and submerged structures
branchWorkflows.procedure: Establish water surface, seabed depth, camera depth and visibility distance separately. For a 24 m reef study, shape a sediment basin, a raised rock shelf and a navigable negative-space channel; leave an open seabed strip so distance attenuation can be judged. Build rock attachment points first, then coral/plant clusters using bounded instances with substrate and slope exclusions. Root plants into sediment and attach hard growth to surfaces; avoid uniformly scattering every organism over every substrate. Model buoyant fronds as curves with primary flow direction and a restrained animated sway, preserving their root attachment. Use rough sediment, distinct rock response and restrained translucent growth. Water absorption/scattering should attenuate with path length; a cyan World tint alone cannot establish depth. Start a bounded volume with declared visibility (for instance 20–40 m for a stylized clear study), then tune against depth markers rather than copying density. Caustics may be a labeled animated light/shader approximation; their presence is not proof of physical caustic simulation. Test up-looking silhouette, side view and a near-to-far marker row under fixed exposure. If the hero vanishes, shorten the optical path or increase local separation before reducing all fog to zero. If growth looks terrestrial, correct support/flow and distribution before adding bubbles. Deliver seabed/reef/growth collections, depth/visibility settings and clear-water/atmosphere images; inspect sediment seams and root attachment without effects.

branchWorkflows.name: Desert dunes, rocky desert and oasis transitions
branchWorkflows.procedure: Choose wind direction and distinguish mobile sand from exposed bedrock. Create a dune cross-section with a broad windward ramp, crest and steeper lee face, then vary ridge continuity; do not repeat identical sine waves across the patch. Put rocks where erosion/exposure explains them and sand drifts against their sheltered sides. For an oasis, define water level, basin and damp-to-dry transition before vegetation. A salt flat, dune field and rocky desert need different surface geometry and roughness, not a sand-color swap. Use broad low-frequency sand form, mid-scale ripples aligned to local wind and fine detail only at the intended pixel scale. Keep ripple normal amplitude below silhouette scale. A low warm sun can reveal crests; a separate high-sun diagnostic reveals overmodeled noise. Heat shimmer belongs to a reversible presentation layer, not deformed delivery geometry. Diagnose toy-sized dunes with a human/vehicle proxy and grain/ripple size comparison. Floating rocks need sand contact repair; razor repeats need ridge variation. Inspect crest silhouette, sheltered dust placement, oasis water edge and a neutral roughness sheet. Deliver wind/height/material masks and a transition section; a still does not prove drifting sand or water behavior.

branchWorkflows.name: Arctic snowfield, glacier and exposed ice
branchWorkflows.procedure: Separate terrain bed, old compacted snow, fresh accumulation, ice and liquid water. Model the terrain first, then accumulate on exposed upward surfaces with authored lee drifts and reduced coverage on steep faces; add roof/overhang exclusion instead of slope-only white paint. For a glacier study, place a directional flow mass, compressed ridges and crevasse openings with modeled depth rather than black decals. Keep hazardous openings visibly distinct from ordinary surface ripples if the game contract requires them. Use rough diffuse snow with subtle subsurface response, smoother blue/clear ice where justified and dirty old snow near traffic. Avoid pure-white clipping that removes terrain form. Compare broad overcast light with low-angle light and preserve a neutral gray-card/height marker. Breath fog is an optional timed effect around the character, not ambient snow shader noise. Snow on cave ceilings requires exposure-mask repair. Plastic ice needs thickness, roughness/reflection and transmission inspection before adding blue saturation. Check footprint/drift scale, sheltered accumulation, crevasse edge continuity and ice-water intersections. Deliver bed and accumulation separately, coverage/thickness masks and both light conditions; snow-motion and engine friction remain untested.

branchWorkflows.name: Jungle canopy, understory and clearing
branchWorkflows.procedure: Build height strata explicitly: a few dominant trunks/crowns, secondary canopy, understory masses, ground cover and decomposing litter. Reserve the actual player/camera route and one light opening before scatter. A 24 m study can contain one canopy gap and one shaded corridor; distribute plants by gap light, moisture and slope. Trunks need root flare/contact, lianas need endpoints and gravity/attachment logic, and epiphytes attach to hosts rather than float in volume. Group crown values into readable masses. Vary leaf roughness by species/wetness without making every leaf a bright mirror. Use canopy-filtered key plus restrained atmospheric shafts; maintain a fog-off leaf/backface diagnostic. Camera height and lens must reveal route clearance and foreground occlusion, not only an overhead attractive carpet. If the image becomes glitter noise, reduce individual leaf contrast/normal strength and consolidate clusters. If the route disappears, change primary canopy/understory placement before merely brightening the floor. Inspect root contact, liana support, clearing silhouette and near/far card appearance. Deliver bounded seeds/masks, strata collections and route-exclusion volumes; target overdraw/performance requires an actual engine test.

branchWorkflows.name: Cave, cavern and inhabited underground
branchWorkflows.procedure: Choose geology or declared fictional formation. Block entrance, main chamber, connecting passage and vertical section with thickness and roof support. Align major strata/fractures before secondary stones. Distinguish water-carved channels, collapse rubble and deposited formations; hanging and rising formations need surface roots. In inhabited caves add practical fixtures, cables, drainage and maintenance access at human scale. Use rough dry rock and localized smoother wet flow, not global wetness. Place daylight only where openings allow it, then motivated lamps or authored bioluminescence. Render a brighter geometry diagnostic: black grading must not conceal missing roof backs, inaccessible passage or wall intersections. Use actual entrance-eye, chamber-eye and reverse cameras. If the chamber looks like a thin tunnel shell, repair roof/side thickness and interlocking masses. If every wall reads as a light source, limit emission to biological/mineral patches. Deliver section, entrance-to-chamber route, dry/wet masks and practical layout. Measure passage gauges and inspect surfaces behind the camera; cave collision, climbing and visibility AI are separate.

branchWorkflows.name: Floating islands and vertical archipelagos
branchWorkflows.procedure: Define the fiction supporting suspension and whether players see/fly below islands. Model the underside as a designed volume with taper, strata, roots and transitions to the top rim; an extruded flat disk with a noisy bottom is insufficient for close underside views. Stage three elevation bands with different silhouettes and preserve unobstructed negative space between them. Bridges, waterfalls and roots need supported origins and explicit endpoints; mark impossible water recirculation as authored fiction rather than geological proof. Top soil/vegetation and underside rock need coherent material continuity. Light the underside enough to reveal construction in a diagnostic, while presentation mist can separate elevation bands. Use a low upward view and a traversal approach as well as the hero wide shot; orthographic and perspective layouts need different overlap checks. If islands merge into one silhouette, alter spacing/height/mass before adding saturated rims. Waterfalls ending in nothing need a deliberate dissolve/out-of-frame boundary. Inspect underside normals, root grounding, bridge anchors and vertical-camera crop. Deliver top/underside modules and altitude/attachment sheet; flight routes and structural feasibility remain project/engine questions.

branchWorkflows.name: Elf and elongated silhouettes
branchWorkflows.procedure: If elongated proportions are requested, lengthen selected torso/limb rhythms coherently rather than uniformly stretching the whole mesh. Block pelvis, rib cage, shoulder and knee landmarks; compare hand reach, seated height and tool grip at the approved total scale. Keep ear design an authored feature with actual attachment/thickness. Use restrained costume planes/material contrast to support long lines, then light from broad side/front to reveal volume. If the figure reads thin/fragile unintentionally, correct mass at joints and torso instead of hiding it with armor. Deliver proportion ratios, neutral/reach/seated poses and ear close-up; ancestry alone must not dictate elegance or personality.

branchWorkflows.name: Dwarf and compact heavy silhouettes
branchWorkflows.procedure: Design compact mass through torso/pelvis/limb ratios and center of visual weight, retaining believable reach for the character's work. Build a tool, workbench and door proxy at that actual body scale. Separate thick costume/armor from underlying joint space; broad forearms and short upper arms need an explicit elbow bend study. Use broad matte/metal groups rather than dense tiny ornament. If tools collide with torso or knees in a working pose, resize/reposition the owned kit or revise approved proportions, not silently shrink the character. Deliver reach/equipment/seat checks and neutral silhouette lineup.

branchWorkflows.name: Orc and goblin alternatives
branchWorkflows.procedure: Treat these as distinct user-authored populations rather than one compulsory jaw/shoulder stereotype. Build alternative mass distributions: a broad high-torso form and a lighter low-center form only if appropriate to the brief. Establish skull/jaw/neck support and hand/foot contact before teeth, spikes or costume. Keep silhouettes readable in grayscale with material roles that do not encode morality. If the only distinction is green skin, revise proportions and authored tools/posture. If large jaw/teeth prevent supplied expressions, repair oral clearance or adapt the design explicitly. Deliver face profile, grip and neutral/action silhouettes with named fictional assumptions.

branchWorkflows.name: Fairy and small winged bodies
branchWorkflows.procedure: Set absolute scale, not just screen size: a 0.2 m figure and a human-sized winged person need different prop/contact cues. Build wing roots, folded/open envelopes and a perch/handhold at that scale. Separate membranes/veins or feather masses from body support; transparency needs a real material/alpha test under the target renderer. Use a backlight plus a neutral opaque-wing diagnostic. If wings vanish, strengthen structural silhouette before increasing emission; if folded wings intersect a costume, repair attachment/hinge envelope. Deliver open/folded/perched views and alpha-on/off comparisons; flight mechanics remain untested.

branchWorkflows.name: Vampire
branchWorkflows.procedure: Build an individual with a chosen predatory/elegant or other approved contrast, not an automatic cape-and-pale-skin package. Establish head/neck profile, mouth/teeth clearance and costume mass around the face. Use one role-specific prop or contact pose to distinguish the individual. Control skin, cloth and metal roughness under neutral light before dramatic rim. If identity disappears without red eyes, strengthen profile/costume proportions. If fangs intersect lips, repair mouth geometry and expression extremes. Deliver neutral and open-mouth/action studies; supernatural lore is supplied fiction rather than a rig capability.

branchWorkflows.name: Werewolf and hybrid limb design
branchWorkflows.procedure: Choose explicit transition between human and animal anatomy, stance and paw/hand use. Block spine/pelvis, digitigrade or plantigrade legs, shoulder rotation and jaw before fur. Use a ground-contact side view and bent-limb proxy to prevent a backward-bending joint illusion. Fur is a separate silhouette layer with a smooth-body diagnostic. If bulk hides knees/elbows, redistribute masses and groom rather than hoping animation will explain them. Deliver anatomy/stance notes, crouch/reach/contact studies and fur-off/on silhouettes. A hybrid appearance is not a verified locomotion or deformation solution.

branchWorkflows.name: Ghost and spectral body
branchWorkflows.procedure: Create a readable opaque source form, then choose missing lower body, trailing cloth or other approved spectral anatomy. Model trails from a stable torso attachment with controlled taper; preserve separate front/back layers to avoid alpha piles. Test opacity and additive/transparent choices against black, gray and bright backgrounds in the actual renderer. If the face disappears or layers sort incorrectly, simplify overlap and restore solid value anchors before more glow. Deliver opaque diagnostic, transparency variants and short motion preview if trails animate; ordinary exports may need baked cards or custom target shaders.

branchWorkflows.name: Zombie and decay asymmetry
branchWorkflows.procedure: Begin from an intact human source and apply a localized, authored damage/decay history. Separate missing volume, displaced cloth, exposed hard parts and staining rather than adding uniform noise. Preserve enough support at weight-bearing joints and enough face structure for required expressions. Use neutral flesh/cloth/material separation, then intended low light. If asymmetry becomes random silhouette clutter, consolidate to one dominant damage direction. If animation exposes unsupported floating parts, repair attachment or identify deliberate supernatural suspension. Deliver intact/decayed pair and joint/face close-ups; gore intensity and anatomy changes remain within the brief.

branchWorkflows.name: Demon and angel heraldic extremes
branchWorkflows.procedure: Define original cosmology and individual role; wings/horns/halos do not mandate morality or copied religious imagery. Build the core body first, then attachment and folded/open envelopes for appendages. Distinguish rigid horns/armor from deforming membranes/feathers. Use large heraldic masses and limited accent material so the face/hands remain legible. If every feature competes, reduce secondary spikes/feathers. If the silhouette clips ordinary doors, supply an alternate folded state or explicitly mark the architecture mismatch. Deliver front/side, appendage states and minimum-screen-size silhouette; ritual meaning and flight remain authored/untested.

branchWorkflows.name: Mutant and beast
branchWorkflows.procedure: Specify one dominant anatomical transformation and its effect on support, movement and tool use. Model a neutral underlying skeleton/mass proxy, then added limbs/growth with explicit attachment and range. Avoid piling unrelated mutations until joint function becomes unintelligible. Use material transitions to show growth versus worn equipment without substituting texture for missing volume. If an extra limb floats or has no working range, repair its root and pose envelope; if the result reads as random noise, return to the primary transformation. Deliver anatomy/attachment section and contact/action studies, marking unverified biological or deformation assumptions.

branchWorkflows.name: Alien morphology
branchWorkflows.procedure: Choose gravity/scale fiction and the character's actual interface needs: locomotion, sensing, communication and manipulation. Block contact/support and a tool/door interface before decorative eyes or surface spots. A nonhuman torso can require different camera/grip landmarks; record them rather than forcing human rig names. Separate skin/chitin/membrane materials with meaningful thickness and test a neutral three-quarter turn. If alien identity is only skin color, revise primary topology/silhouette. If proportions prevent the requested task, repair the owned interface/design explicitly. Deliver functional pose sheet and human-scale comparison; no biological or rig-compatibility claim.

branchWorkflows.name: Cybernetic body
branchWorkflows.procedure: Choose which systems are replaced and where organic/synthetic transitions occur. Build socket, seal, fastening/service access and flexible connection at each transition; do not merely draw glowing seams on skin. Keep cables outside joint crush zones and plates clear of bend envelopes. Neutral light should distinguish skin, coating and bare metal; emission is a separate status layer. If the elbow locks visually, split plates/reposition flex sections. Deliver cover-on/off and bent/rest views plus interface landmarks; motor/control function remains unimplemented unless separately built.

branchWorkflows.name: Robot and android
branchWorkflows.procedure: Decide whether mechanical construction is visible or human mimicry is the goal. Robots need articulated joints, bearings/clearance, covers and service openings; androids need deliberate skin/face transitions and expression compatibility. Use rigidly attached parts where appropriate instead of smooth skinning every plate. Compare opaque/emission-off silhouettes and joint extremes with a consistent scale camera. If the robot is a featureless suit, add meaningful separation/service logic; if the android becomes uncanny unintentionally, inspect face proportions/material scale before grading. Deliver mechanical/skin layer map, rest/bend/face states and explicit rig handoff.

branchWorkflows.name: Mecha and pilot scale
branchWorkflows.procedure: Lock mech height and pilot/operator size independently. Block cockpit/control/maintenance access, feet/contact and main limb swept volumes before armor fins. Include a pilot proxy near the hatch and service ladder so scale survives a hero shot. Separate frame, actuators and armor; test knee/hip/shoulder clearance with an exploded diagram. If it reads as a human-sized robot, revise hatch/handrail/panel scale cues; if armor intersects, repair the local envelope rather than shrinking the pilot. Use broad coating and restrained metal/emission under neutral and dramatic light. Deliver pilot-access, service and pose sheets; walking balance or structural feasibility is not established.

branchWorkflows.name: Chibi body treatment
branchWorkflows.procedure: Treat chibi as a proportion/style choice compatible with any individual role. Set head/body ratio and actual height, then preserve readable hands, feet and face at minimum screen size. Build tool grips and seated/bent states because a large head/short arm can obstruct reach. Use broad material/value groups and simple highlights; fine surface noise usually competes with the silhouette. If the head clips shoulders or props, adjust local shapes/pose range within the approved style. Deliver equal-scale proportion sheet and thumbnail expressions; do not claim adult/child age from head ratio alone.

branchWorkflows.name: Knight
branchWorkflows.procedure: Build armor by articulation zones: torso shell, shoulder, upper/lower limb plates and flexible joints. Fit a shield/weapon to actual hand/grip, then test raised arm, seated and crouched proxies. Distinguish coating, bare edges and cloth without making all armor uniformly silver. If the elbow bridges, split/overlap plates with bend clearance. Deliver armor-layer and grip sheets plus neutral/action silhouettes; a rigid pose study is not a tested deformation rig.

branchWorkflows.name: Samurai
branchWorkflows.procedure: Choose a supplied or researched date/culture and distinguish historical reconstruction from fantasy. Block armor/garment layers and attachment before ornaments, then test seated/kneeling and weapon/sheath clearance with the body. Keep rigid plates and flexible ties separate. If unsupported motifs or mixed equipment appear, replace or label them rather than treating a broad role name as evidence. Neutral side light should reveal layering. Deliver dated feature ledger when fidelity matters and layer/working-pose views.

branchWorkflows.name: Ninja and covert specialist
branchWorkflows.procedure: Use the actual role/context instead of assuming a universal historical black costume. Build mobility-oriented clothing, carry system and one supplied tool with stowed/deployed states. Test crouch, climb/reach and hand access to storage. Separate cloth fold mass from rigid equipment. If the role vanishes without dark color, strengthen loadout/pose and task-specific silhouette. Deliver equipment-state and reach views; concealment, climbing or historical authenticity needs its own evidence.

branchWorkflows.name: Pirate
branchWorkflows.procedure: Establish maritime task and era/fantasy level, then build clothing compatible with that work and a small equipment kit with reachable carry points. Test rope/tool grip and deck stance rather than stacking unrelated skull/weapon motifs. Distinguish salt/water-exposed wear from protected lining. If a coat/weapon intersects the working hand or deck, repair attachment/length. Deliver stowed/working states and period assumptions; sailing/combat behavior is outside the asset study.

branchWorkflows.name: Cowboy and frontier worker
branchWorkflows.procedure: Choose occupation, locality/date and activity such as mounted work or repair. Fit hat/outerwear, boots, tool belt and a role-specific item to the approved body, then check seated/mounted proxy and arm reach. Use cloth/leather/metal groups with handling wear, avoiding dust on every protected surface. If accessories collide with the saddle/seat or obscure hands, repair carry points. Deliver standing/seated/action silhouettes and sourced exceptions when historical fidelity is required.

branchWorkflows.name: Soldier
branchWorkflows.procedure: Obtain year/organization/role and loadout constraints before modeling. Build garment base, protective equipment and carry modules around actual access/weight distribution, with neutral unmarked source if markings are unverified. Test crouch, prone-like proxy and shoulder reach as requested, without claiming tactics or equipment function. If pouches block joints/grip, move local mounts. Deliver dated inventory, attachment sheet and neutral/action views; costume readability does not prove operational suitability.

branchWorkflows.name: Detective
branchWorkflows.procedure: Define setting and investigative task rather than defaulting to a trench coat. Build one evidence/tool interaction and reachable storage, with clothing mass supporting face/hand visibility. Compare relaxed and focused working poses at the story camera. Use restrained material accents on the tool, not glow on every pocket. If the role is only a hat, strengthen the action/loadout and prop state. Deliver seated/standing/tool-close-up views and continuity landmarks for narrative shots.

branchWorkflows.name: Assassin
branchWorkflows.procedure: Use original role fiction and supplied movement; do not let it dictate morality or one cultural costume. Build a compact carry system, task-specific tool and deploy/stow states around joint clearance. Test reach and silhouette from the intended camera, keeping ornamental cloth clear of the hand/action. If a long silhouette element intersects the ground or conceals required motion, adjust its owned attachment/length. Deliver rest/action/stowed states; stealth/detection and weapon behavior remain untested.

branchWorkflows.name: Mercenary
branchWorkflows.procedure: Define service history and equipment procurement so a mixed kit has a reason. Build a maintained core with a few mismatched replacements sharing plausible attachment interfaces. Separate recent repair from old wear and retain an unmarked variant. If every piece has unrelated scale/technology, unify mounts, manufacturing rhythm and primary material groups. Deliver loadout inventory, repair-state close-ups and working-pose clearances; visual history does not establish combat performance.

branchWorkflows.name: Superhero
branchWorkflows.procedure: Design an original dominant silhouette and symbol system around the stated abilities and identity. Build suit/armor/appendages as layers, with a neutral civilian-scale proxy where useful. Test cape/wing/large emblem clearance and hand/face read in a signature pose and relaxed pose. If emission or saturated color alone carries recognition, strengthen large forms. Deliver clean/emission-off and action silhouettes plus attachment states; supernatural capability is fiction, not simulated evidence.

branchWorkflows.name: Villain or antagonist
branchWorkflows.procedure: Start from individual role and story function instead of equating disability, ethnicity or body type with evil. Choose a distinct authority/tool/costume hierarchy and build its actual attachments/use state. Contrast primary masses and one deliberate asymmetry only when the brief supports it. If the result relies on generic spikes/black palette, refine occupation and face/hand hierarchy. Deliver neutral and story-action views with the approved symbol/material system; audience reaction is not measurable from a single render.

branchWorkflows.name: Witch
branchWorkflows.procedure: Use the supplied cultural/fantasy context and actual practice, not compulsory caricature. Build a portable or stationary working kit with containers, tool grips and active/inactive ritual elements. Test hand access, seated/kneeling posture and long clothing clearance. Separate ordinary fabric/wood/metal from any magical material. If every prop glows, reserve emission for the current action and reveal ordinary construction. Deliver working-kit layout, rest/action and magic-off views, preserving original lore and rights.

branchWorkflows.name: Wizard
branchWorkflows.procedure: Define what the character does with magic and how the kit supports it: staff/book/instrument are options, not mandatory. Build grip/opening/pivot states for the chosen focus and clothing layers around arm reach. A book needs thickness, hinge and page block; a staff needs hand/ground clearance. If the focus hides the face or clips the shoulder, repair staging and attachment before changing body scale. Deliver readable thumbnail silhouette, prop-state sheet and neutral/magic comparison; effects and game ability logic are separate handoffs.

branchWorkflows.name: Medieval-inspired low magic
branchWorkflows.procedure: Choose a specific local construction vocabulary from approved references; do not make dirt, European timber or a particular religion compulsory. Build one inhabited bay with load-bearing posts/wall core, roof support, doorway, drainage and a repair patch. Repeat it through an inside corner and roof junction. For a proposed two-meter module, preserve wall/roof connection planes while letting hand-crafted edges vary inside those bounds. Add a functional daily-life station such as storage, cooking or repair with plausible hand access and tool scale. Use timber grain along members, stone/plaster as separate layers and iron fittings where mechanically meaningful. Metal straps should wrap or fasten parts rather than float on them. Light primarily through the opening and task practical; check neutral material response before warm grade. Inspect joinery cutaway, doorstep/handle height and roof seam. Uniform grime needs exposure/use masks; miniature-looking buildings need wall/beam and prop scale correction. Deliver modular connections and one repaired/intact pair; historical accuracy requires its own sources, and fantasy does not establish it.

branchWorkflows.name: High fantasy and magical infrastructure
branchWorkflows.procedure: First define how magic changes construction, water, transport or illumination. Model source → conduit → receiver → service access and an inactive state. A crystal-powered bridge needs anchored terminals, a coherent span/field vocabulary and a route visible when emission is disabled; crystals scattered on generic masonry do not establish infrastructure. Scale a monumental portal around a smaller actual human doorway if both ceremony and habitation matter. Repeat heraldic motifs through structural silhouettes before surface engravings. Keep stone, metal and emissive energy physically distinguishable. Limit luminous accents to functional nodes and preserve ordinary reflection/roughness so the inactive scene reads. Stage a heroic wide view, an arrival view and a maintenance close-up. If bloom erases heraldry, reduce emission/glare and improve source geometry. If a floating span appears accidentally unsupported, author a visible magical support rule or change the construction. Deliver active/inactive assemblies, service-chain diagram and connection/clearance notes; shader effects and bridge gameplay need separate target implementation.

branchWorkflows.name: Dark fantasy, corruption and ruined grandeur
branchWorkflows.procedure: Specify prior purpose, damage cause and elapsed state before adding thorns/ash. Build an intact structural bay, create a recoverable damaged derivative and place rubble consistent with the breach. Corruption should follow an authored cause: roots pry joints, mineral growth follows seepage or supernatural tissue connects to a source. Vary the mechanism across primary/secondary scale instead of wrapping every surface in identical spikes. Retain human-scale stairs/handles against monumental masses. Use broad value separation between actors, floor and background; dark fantasy need not be featureless black or compulsory gore. Separate ash, rust, wet stone and organic growth masks. A low key and sparse practicals can express mood, but maintain a brighter diagnostic and corruption-off view. Repair collapsed silhouettes through mass/lighting, not only outlines. Inspect supported broken slabs, doorway gauge and readable threat-free route markers. Deliver intact/damaged/corrupted states and their chronology; atmosphere alone cannot prove narrative or encounter quality.

branchWorkflows.name: Urban fantasy: concealed and public magic
branchWorkflows.procedure: Retain the established city's building date, utilities and ordinary movement first. Add a hidden magical layer at service thresholds, basement access or selected signage; public magic instead needs visible distribution, maintenance and everyday adaptation. Build one modern frontage, ordinary entrance, magical threshold and interior/back-side service junction. Show who can see/use the threshold through supplied art rules rather than inventing access logic. Contrast modern finish and old relic craft while keeping contact, scale and mounting plausible. A sigil projected on a wall, engraved into it and built as luminous tubing need different geometry/material treatment. Compare daylight ordinary-use, night magical and emission-off views from the same camera. If neon overwhelms city identity, reduce its area and retain ordinary window/street-light hierarchy. If hidden access cannot be found under the approved visibility rules, repair its authored signifier, not the game rules. Deliver mundane/magical variants and threshold states; urban lore, concealment logic and engine transitions remain explicit handoffs.

branchWorkflows.name: Lateral fighting game
branchWorkflows.procedure: Block the actual lateral action plane, camera range and stage boundaries before background dressing. Place two actors at center and extreme separation, including crouch/jump/long reach poses from the supplied animation envelope. Build the floor contact strip with a stable horizon and reserve quiet values behind heads/hands. Background pillars can be richly staged outside the playable plane but must not merge with weapon silhouettes at common positions. Test camera center and both frame edges at minimum output size, with flat actors and effects off/on. If feet disappear into floor pattern, reduce pattern contrast and clarify contact shadows rather than changing actor height. If the widest pose crops, repair owned camera/stage framing within the agreed contract. Deliver floor/boundary modules, pose/frame-edge contact sheet and background depth diagram; this does not validate collision boxes, frame timing or competitive balance.

branchWorkflows.name: Beat 'em up and depth-lane brawler
branchWorkflows.procedure: Build a shallow depth arena with multiple actor feet visible at near/far positions. Specify whether decorative steps are usable height or background only. Stage a door/arrival, one obstacle and a breakable family with consistent depth cues, keeping the action floor comparatively quiet. Use contact shadows and perspective scale to reveal depth without painting false lane boundaries unless requested. Keep floor detail from resembling interaction/hazard cues. Inspect reverse approach, high/low cameras and neutral silhouette maps. Deliver state/arrival sheet and sampled geometric sightline diagram; symmetry or ray visibility does not prove fairness or map balance.

branchWorkflows.name: Monumental inhabited ruins
branchWorkflows.procedure: Block one large structural bay around human-scale steps, handles, door inserts and usable routes. Separate ceremonial silhouette from actual opening/contact dimensions. Build an intact master, then damaged/abandoned or repaired derivative with coherent support and exposure history. A 24 m tall study should still explain how a person enters and where floors/landings lie. Use broad stone/metal/organic value groups and restrained practicals, with a bright neutral cutaway. If the actor disappears into grey stone, repair large-value/light separation before adding an outline or fog. If doors look usable at impossible scale, add a smaller entrance or identify ceremonial framing. Deliver human/monument sections, intact/derived pair and eye/hero views; structural stability and encounter challenge are not established.

branchWorkflows.name: Vertical loops and remembered shortcuts
branchWorkflows.procedure: Build lower arrival, upper return and a persistent landmark visible from both levels. Use supplied stairs/elevator/ladders as shell/proxy contracts; measure matching landings and opening heights. Stage the shortcut so its relation to the original arrival can be understood visually without a label. Keep intermediate shaft/interior/back sides modeled where cameras can see them. Test entry, upper reveal and reverse-return cameras with atmosphere disabled. If an elevator opening floats above its landing, repair geometry/state rather than inventing a lift behavior. If the landmark is lost in the upper view, alter its outline or occluding masses. Deliver vertical section, landing measurements and paired remembered-view images. This cannot prove that a lift operates, a shortcut unlocks or progression is connected in the game.

branchWorkflows.name: Rest landmark and safe-space contrast
branchWorkflows.procedure: Use supplied safe/rest vocabulary; build a recognizable object/place and active/inactive states with stable interaction anchor. Surround it with a quieter composition, some human-scale use trace and distinct material/light hierarchy. Safe space can be daylight, shelter or a practical light pool; it need not be warm orange or a fire. Inspect return approach and minimum screen size in grayscale/emission-off. If the marker is indistinguishable from decoration, strengthen physical frame/negative space. If every practical uses the same safe-state cue, differentiate ordinary fixtures. Deliver state/anchor sheet and arrival/return views. Art cues do not establish saving, healing or actual enemy exclusion.

branchWorkflows.name: Mist thresholds and encounter readability
branchWorkflows.procedure: Build an original threshold frame with explicit opening, mist layer/volume and active/inactive state. Keep the frame recognizable when mist is dense and model the route beyond sufficiently for requested views. Test the largest supplied actor/weapon silhouette at camera edges and behind local obstructions, with effects off/on. If fog hides both frame and actor, reduce coverage or revise lighting/mass separation rather than declare ambiguity intentional. If floor cracks resemble danger cues, quiet the pattern. Deliver threshold state pairs, actor-edge contact sheet and obstruction samples. Difficulty never justifies falsely claiming invisible hazards or broken camera art passed; combat fairness and fog-gate behavior need actual runtime/playtest evidence.

branchWorkflows.name: Shadow-lane infiltration
branchWorkflows.procedure: Build a lit crossing and sheltered perimeter using actual standing/crouched eye/clearance dimensions. Place practical fixtures with visible mounting and a reason for the light pool; include the route's entry and exit in the study. Keep shadow transitions legible without making essential geometry black. A brighter diagnostic should expose all walls, openings and contacts. Test player/guard-eye samples and both stance heights, with static cone overlays separately. If exposure crushing hides a ledge or corner, repair local material/light separation. If an apparently opaque hedge has open proxy intent, reconcile art and contract instead of asserting safety. Deliver lit/diagnostic views and labeled sample geometry; AI visibility and moving patrol detection remain unverified.

branchWorkflows.name: Social infiltration and access states
branchWorkflows.procedure: When the brief relies on clothing, credentials or public/private space, build thresholds, counters, barriers and staff/service routes rather than simply adding darkness. Define approved visitor/staff/restricted visual states and identifiable access hardware. Keep an ordinary public path readable and show both sides of the checkpoint at human scale. Use architectural/material hierarchy and role-specific props without assuming one uniform or culture universally signifies permission. If every door appears equally restricted, revise threshold shape/state accents. If a barrier blocks actual staff circulation, repair its opening/placement. Deliver access-state and reverse-view sheet; credentials, authorization and social AI are separate systems, not inferred from props.

branchWorkflows.name: Vertical entry, vents and ledges
branchWorkflows.procedure: Use supplied actor envelope, climb/reach and camera sweep. Build vent opening, internal bend, exit, ladder/ledge or requested hardware as actual volumes, not a small facade grille. Include attachment/fastener and hand/foot contact cues appropriate to the construction. Stowed/open covers need their own swept bounds. Inspect approach/entry/interior/exit plus a side section. If the vent is too small, enlarge the authorized architecture or mark it decorative—never shrink the actor silently. If the camera sees through missing backs, complete the volume. Deliver dimensions, open/closed states and contact/camera samples. A gauge fit is not proof of crawling, climbing or camera collision.

branchWorkflows.name: Noise-material and distraction-prop vocabulary
branchWorkflows.procedure: Use actual game sound classes to choose distinct visual families such as grates, carpet, standing water or loose debris. Model thickness/edge/contact so materials read from the intended camera, with roughness and shape rather than color alone. Build a distraction prop with intact/used or moving/rest state only as supplied, keeping grip/throw or activation anchor explicit. If a loud-looking grate is classified silent by the game, report and reconcile the cue rather than changing audio rules. If every bottle/container looks interactable, differentiate decoration/state grammar. Deliver material-state sheet and close/far views, with sound/detection behavior explicitly untested. Static sight cones and material labels are interface proposals, not executed stealth mechanics.

branchWorkflows.name: Real-time strategy (RTS)
branchWorkflows.procedure: Build three supplied functions as different roof/mass silhouettes before team color: for example a storage volume, production structure and observation structure if those functions exist. Add neutral, team and damaged states with identical footprint/anchor. Place unit-size proxies around entrances and rally/service side; keep animated appendage envelopes separate from occupied tiles. Reserve a broad team-color panel rather than tinting every material. Render near/far and selected/unselected with a grayscale version and UI overlays. If function survives only a tiny sign, alter the large roof/functional shape. If team hue makes functions indistinguishable, reduce color area and restore value/mass separation. Deliver footprint/overhang/selection layers, state sheet and far-camera images; these do not prove unit navigation or production behavior.

branchWorkflows.name: Turn-based strategy (square and hex)
branchWorkflows.procedure: Select actual grid coordinates, tile size, elevation steps and legal rotations. Build center, edge, corner and height-transition tiles plus one unit/structure occupancy study. Hex tiles need the exact orientation and neighbor offsets; a square-grid rotation recipe is not interchangeable. Keep terrain art irregularity inside agreed boundary/connection planes and label intentional overhangs. Use subdued terrain values with distinct boundary/selection treatment supplied by UI, not permanent bright edges on all geometry. Inspect adjacent tile combinations, tall-object occlusion and far zoom from the actual projection. If a cliff decoration hides a selected cell, lower/reposition art or provide the approved cutaway variant. Deliver neighbor/rotation sheet and elevation sections; movement costs, range and turn rules require the target implementation.

branchWorkflows.name: Tower defense
branchWorkflows.procedure: Model path, build pad, tower base and entrance/exit markers as distinct families. Use the supplied lane width and tower footprint; keep attack-range circles and enemy envelopes in diagnostic collections. Build tower upgrade stages with the same socket/pivot and identify barrel/rotor overhang at each stage. A tall upgraded tower must not accidentally cover an adjacent pad in the intended camera. Separate route surface, buildable ground and decorative border by form/value as well as hue. Test a crowded tower cluster with effects disabled, then with worst-case supplied effect proxies. If paths resemble build pads, repair construction grammar; if towers hide enemies, adjust silhouette/height staging within approved bounds. Deliver upgrade states, pad/path join sheet and camera comparisons, with range, targeting and enemy flow explicitly untested.

branchWorkflows.name: MOBA lanes and structures
branchWorkflows.procedure: Obtain lane/jungle/objective vocabulary and the actual camera/character scale. Build lane edge, vegetation/concealment family, tower/objective base and landmark as modular pieces. Keep function and faction identity separate and preserve consistent interaction footprint through active/damaged/destroyed states. Stage allied/enemy-size proxies on both approaches; reverse views matter even with a nominal fixed camera. Reserve floor quietness around action; team colors belong in controlled zones and broad value contrast should keep units legible. If vegetation falsely implies guaranteed concealment, reconcile its art with the supplied visibility proxy and label the static scope. If tower rubble resembles live tower base, differentiate destroyed state shape. Deliver lane/jungle/objective state and far-camera sheets; navigation, fog-of-war and combat balance are not inferred from the layout.

branchWorkflows.name: City builder
branchWorkflows.procedure: Choose lot/grid and road/service connector contracts. Build a representative residence, service and industrial function with front/back access, utility attachment and low/high-density state. Roofs and large functional parts must identify use at far zoom. Place building anchor and road connector independently when required; disclose roof/canopy overhang beyond the lot rather than silently clipping it. Use regional material coherence while reserving service/state accents. Render joined lots, inside/outside road corners and crowded blocks from zoom extremes. If doors face inaccessible rear lots, fix connector orientation; if tall buildings hide required streets, provide approved cutaway/height alternatives rather than claiming pathfinding handles it. Deliver lot/connector data, density states and adjacent-block visual tests; service coverage, traffic and simulation performance need engine evidence.

branchWorkflows.name: Colony simulation
branchWorkflows.procedure: Treat each workstation/room as a use sequence: approach, worker position, input storage, operating space and output/storage. Build furniture/equipment with occupied and idle state and a roof/wall cutaway strategy for the supplied camera. Keep bed/door/tool interactions aligned to the actual pawn size. Shelves/doors that animate need both open envelopes and collision intent identified. Differentiate work, rest and storage by large forms, with modest material accents. If a roof makes activity invisible, implement the approved removable/cutaway art state. If workstation clutter fills the worker slot, move it before increasing the room size. Deliver interaction-marker and state sheet plus crowded-room review; scheduling, needs and job/economy behavior remain external.

branchWorkflows.name: Life simulation
branchWorkflows.procedure: Build a domestic interaction set at the supplied body scale: seat/table/storage or requested equivalents, with sitting/standing/reach markers and open/closed states. Coordinate seat height, knee/arm clearance and door swing using actual proxies. Decorative bounds should not impersonate interaction bounds. Keep variants sharing attachment landmarks so recolors and upgrades do not shift hands/feet. Use friendly or realistic style from the project, not a compulsory pastel palette. Inspect seated eye-level and actual game camera, including wall cutaway when needed. If a cabinet opens through a chair or users float above seats, repair pivot/marker geometry. Deliver interaction landmarks, state poses and assembly measurements; animation alignment and navigation still require runtime checks.

branchWorkflows.name: Farming simulation
branchWorkflows.procedure: Choose plot dimensions, row direction and tool/harvest vocabulary. Build soil dry/wet/tilled states and at least seedling/growing/ready/harvested crop variants if those states exist. Keep root/pivot anchored to plot coordinates through growth; expanded foliage must have a declared overhang and avoid hiding neighboring readiness. Model irrigation/storage/tool access as separate assets with plausible junctions. Use growth-state silhouette and value differences before reliance on color/glow. Test dense adjacent plots, target zoom and low-light collection view. If mature canopy conceals plot borders, group/lift/reduce leaves or adjust approved camera; if tools do not reach the row, repair owned dimensions/handles. Deliver state lineup, plot/irrigation connector sheet and harvest-proxy views; yield, timing and watering logic are unimplemented.

branchWorkflows.name: Other simulation/process assets
branchWorkflows.procedure: For a requested simulation outside these families, decompose the visible process into input, storage, operation, output and service states before modeling. Record which dimensions and states come from the actual system and which are visual proposals. Build one representative loop and all transition geometry, including expanded/open bounds. Use clearly named source/state variants rather than embedding logic claims in model names. Inspect actual actor/tool contact and final camera, with status colors disabled to ensure form still communicates use. A pipeline that appears connected needs connector measurement; a plausible machine cannot be called functional. Deliver process/state diagram, interface anchors and unresolved runtime tests. branchWorkflows.name: Urban salvage and container language

Create intact/open/stripped/repaired variants with consistent hinges/pivots and recognizable silhouettes. Separate old exposure damage from fresh scavenging marks and current repair. branchWorkflows.name: Western frontier and settled town
branchWorkflows.procedure: Choose actual settlement, decade and building use before selecting a cinematic false-front vocabulary. Build one frontage as wall structure, cladding, roof/back side, doorway and walkway; include a service/delivery side rather than a facade-only stage. Add a dated daily prop and horse/cart/person proxy only where the brief requires them. Check board/beam dimensions and fasteners against sources, preserving repeated-bay connection planes. Use exposure-dependent dust/paint wear and hand-contact polish, not universal orange grading. Inspect neutral daylight, street-eye and rear construction views. A miniature appearance needs timber/tool scale repair; an unsupported veranda needs actual supports/joinery. branchWorkflows.name: Pirate and maritime port
branchWorkflows.procedure: Specify region, ship/port use and date rather than assembling every skull, cannon and sail motif. Build a dock slice with tide/water level, piles, decking, mooring attachment and cargo path. For a ship component define deck curvature, rail and rigging attachment from chosen evidence; rope must reach belaying/anchoring points and respect gravity. Keep working access around hatches and lines. Differentiate wet splash-zone wood, drier sheltered surfaces, rope and metal corrosion. Test low dock-eye and vessel-eye views plus an attachment close-up. If cargo blocks the entire working path, revise staging; floating ropes need endpoint/tension correction. Deliver waterline/tide assumptions and separate dock/rope/cargo collections. Sailing feasibility and marine engineering remain outside art inspection.

branchWorkflows.name: Japanese warrior-era setting and infiltration fiction
branchWorkflows.procedure: Choose locality/date/social setting and distinguish researched architecture from later entertainment shorthand. Build a gate/room bay with documented structural rhythm, floor transition, roof edge and movable screen/door mechanism. Use a human proxy to test opening/threshold and equipment display clearance. If a ninja/infiltration route is requested, add only approved vents/ledges/access hardware consistent with the chosen construction or explicitly label alternate history. Keep timber, plaster/paper/roof finish and metal fittings distinct according to references. Inspect neutral front/side and open/closed states before dramatic moonlight. Generic mixed-century armor or motifs need replacement or a declared fictional blend, not a widened date label. Deliver construction/state sheet and feature sources; Blender shadows do not validate stealth.

branchWorkflows.name: Viking-age or other Scandinavian period
branchWorkflows.procedure: Do not infer one universal hall/ship/costume from the broad label. Select settlement/use/date and build a structural bay, roof support, hearth/work area and doorway from references. Keep occupation-scale objects and tool storage accessible. If a maritime element is included, document its own source rather than transferring every building ornament onto a hull. Use material layering and localized soot/wear tied to the selected ventilation/hearth arrangement. A bright neutral cutaway should expose support and circulation; atmospheric firelight is an additional view. If carved detail overwhelms documented plain structure, reduce it. Deliver roof/wall junction, everyday prop and evidence exceptions; mythology and fantasy belong to explicitly named variants.

branchWorkflows.name: Ancient Egypt
branchWorkflows.procedure: Choose period, locality and domestic/administrative/ceremonial function; monumental stone, ordinary buildings and interiors need different evidence. Construct wall core/finish, opening/lintel and a repeated bay with a human-scale insert. Add a source-backed furnishing/container rather than coating every object in gold. Keep any undeciphered/unsourced inscription as a clearly labeled neutral placeholder shape, not fabricated authentic text. Separate stone/finish, textiles and metal/leaf layers. Compare ungraded sun/shade and construction section; museum aging is not necessarily use-time appearance. If the model is an undifferentiated sand-colored block, restore sourced surface/structural divisions. Deliver feature ledger and proposed versus supported polychromy variants without declaring authenticity from rendering quality.

branchWorkflows.name: Ancient Greece
branchWorkflows.procedure: Specify date/place/building type and a particular source for proportions/details. Build base, support, beam/roof junction and wall/enclosure as separate elements; repeat the bay through a corner before adding ornament. Do not combine different orders/details by convenience unless the brief names an invented hybrid. Include everyday scale and access, not only a temple hero shot. Treat weathered museum marble and reconstructed painted/finished surfaces as different evidence states. Use neutral side light to inspect profile continuity and seams. If a repeated column/capital changes scale at corners, repair shared module dimensions. Deliver profile/source sheet, junction and finish assumptions; proportional plausibility is not archaeological verification.

branchWorkflows.name: Ancient Rome
branchWorkflows.procedure: Choose date/place/function and research wall core, facing, roof/vault and service details independently. Model a bay section that explains structure beneath decorative facing, with doorway/drainage and human use. Mosaic/floor panels need actual region/scale and gutters; do not randomly mix symbols from unrelated sites. Build a broken/cutaway derivative without destroying the intact master. Separate core, plaster/stone facing, metal and floor finish. Inspect neutral cutaway, floor grazing angle and entry view; a shiny marble coating alone cannot establish the setting. Floating facades need connection/edge repair. Deliver supported versus reconstructed finish states and ledger; do not imply that a decorative arch model proves structural stability.

branchWorkflows.name: Victorian and industrial urban settings
branchWorkflows.procedure: Select city, decade, class/use and technology before choosing brick, iron, wallpaper or glass. Build one repeated facade/interior bay with floor structure, opening, drainage and service access. A machinery insert needs power/transmission and operator clearance at the chosen scale. Keep mass-produced versus handmade details internally consistent with evidence. Use distinct brick/mortar, painted wood, metal and paper finishes with wear at use/exposure. Test daylight window response and practical-lit interior separately. Mixed modern fittings require verification or removal. Deliver facade/corner/service junction and dated furnishing sheet; aesthetic industrial richness alone does not establish period accuracy.

branchWorkflows.name: Modern civilian setting
branchWorkflows.procedure: Bound the decade/locality and building function; modern is not a single worldwide kit. Construct facade/enclosure, access/service panels and a daily-use object with documented dimensions or explicit design proposals. Keep accessibility/code claims separate unless actual requirements are supplied and checked. Show power/communication/maintenance routing only where the brief needs it. Use finish/manufacturing consistency, restrained dirt and legible product-state variants. Inspect human-eye, service-open and neutral material views. If all equipment differs in manufacturing era, reconcile the procurement/history rather than applying uniform wear. Deliver date/source/assumption ledger and state kit; code compliance and equipment function remain unverified without their own tests.

branchWorkflows.name: World War I-era military kit
branchWorkflows.procedure: Name year, theater, side/unit and role; verify clothing/webbing, helmet, tools, transport and markings as separate evidence items. Build a mannequin/loadout or emplacement slice from those sources with actual attachment and reachable storage. Avoid copying later optics/rails or treating every vehicle as interchangeable. Preserve a neutral unmarked variant until markings are verified. Separate canvas/leather/metal/paint according to the chosen kit and place wear by handling/environment. Inspect silhouette, attachment close-up and equipment-overlap poses. Unsupported pieces need replacement or an alternate-history label. Deliver the dated inventory and uncertainties; asset inspection is neither equipment-function nor tactical advice/testing.

branchWorkflows.name: World War II-era military kit
branchWorkflows.procedure: Repeat the year/theater/unit/role discipline rather than reusing a generic earlier kit. Establish which production variant and service state the references show. Build mounting brackets, stowage and crew access for vehicle/equipment sets; keep repeated parts at consistent manufacturing scale. Match camouflage/markings to the selected evidence and preserve an unmarked master. Review neutral paint/cloth/metal response, profile and occupied/service-open views. A correctly shaped shell with incompatible attachments still fails the dated contract. Repair the specific mismatch rather than adding battle damage to obscure it. Deliver component/date ledger and crew-clearance study; no operational or historical-authenticity conclusion without adequate sources.

Analog/digital display and recording equipment need source-backed combinations. Use coating, plastic/rubber, metal and textile finishes appropriate to the selected objects; avoid making all older equipment rusty. Test screen-off and screen-on with readable controls and neutral scale views. Anachronistic modern connectors require evidence, replacement or explicit fictional retrofit. Deliver base/retrofit variants with the retrofit boundary identified; neither a working-looking control panel nor its labels establish functionality.

branchWorkflows.name: Hard science fiction
branchWorkflows.procedure: Write gravity, pressure, crew/service scale, power and thermal assumptions. Build a habitat/service bay around a human proxy: pressure boundary, access hatch, replaceable panel, connector and equipment withdrawal envelope. Separate structural frame from covers. Route cables/pipes between actual terminals, place fasteners where covers can open and show an exposed maintenance state. In zero-g fiction provide handholds and orientation cues rather than gratuitous floor clutter; in rotating/artificial gravity show its declared direction consistently. Use subdued coatings, bare metal only where appropriate and small status indicators separated from structural emission. Neutral side light should expose panel depth and seals. If detail becomes meaningless greebles, remove elements without attachment/service purpose. If a hatch intersects its frame or equipment cannot be withdrawn, repair the mechanism envelope. Deliver pressure/structure/service layer diagram, closed/open states and crew-eye review. These are visual consistency checks, not pressure-vessel or radiation certification.

branchWorkflows.name: Space opera
branchWorkflows.procedure: Establish symbolic scale and faction form language before microdetail. Block a monumental hangar/ship silhouette with a small repeated crew/access element to communicate size. Build primary keel/tower/engine masses, secondary bays and only then antennas, surface panels and hero insignia. Keep a service-scale interior insert separate from ceremonial exterior openings if their scales differ intentionally. Use material/value groups to preserve silhouette at distant camera; emissive engines should not bleach hull panels. Compare hero wide, distant black silhouette and maintenance-eye detail. If scale shifts between shots, fix repeated windows/doors and detail frequency rather than claiming every tiny panel is huge. Deliver scale sheet and near/far variants, with fictional technology labeled. Dramatic scale does not justify accidental floating parts, source destruction or false engine-performance claims.

branchWorkflows.name: Cyberpunk
branchWorkflows.procedure: Organize tower, street and service strata with deliberate access and infrastructure. A 12 m alley study can include occupied frontage, overhead utility rack, public sign, repair stall and a quieter destination. Model sign brackets, cable sag/endpoints, drainage and repair layers. Reserve pedestrian/camera clearance before adding hanging cables or umbrellas. Vertical density must retain readable hierarchy from street eye and an elevated view. Use wet response by substrate, controlled luminous signage and ordinary shadow-side surfaces. Keep original sign faces/emissive materials independent so animation does not affect building walls. If neon alone supplies identity, strengthen stacked massing and service history. If reflections erase the route, reduce saturated area/roughness extremes and inspect dry/emission-off versions. Deliver dry/wet and sign active/inactive states; political narratives and city systems follow the supplied brief rather than the genre name.

branchWorkflows.name: Steampunk
branchWorkflows.procedure: Define steam source, working machine, exhaust/condensate route and service access. Build boiler-like mass, pipes with coherent diameters/bends, valve/gauge station and driven mechanism as distinct assemblies. Use brackets and flange/fastener logic; do not attach every pipe to nowhere. Show one open maintenance cover and a stopped state. A decorative gauge is not a measured operating instrument. Separate painted iron/steel structure from copper/brass fittings and worn hand-contact parts. Warm light can support the palette but inspect neutral metal response. If everything reads as gold plastic, correct conductor masks, roughness and reflections. If moving rods intersect housings, repair pivots/envelopes or label the mechanism static/decorative. Deliver source-to-work diagram, component pivots and stopped/working visual states; no pressure or machine feasibility claim.

branchWorkflows.name: Dieselpunk
branchWorkflows.procedure: Choose a coherent retro-industrial reference vocabulary instead of combining unrelated military eras. Build a heavy powertrain housing, frame rails, vents, access doors and fuel/service elements with readable load-bearing versus replaceable parts. An oversized grille needs an actual behind-grille volume; exhaust and intake must be visually distinct. Keep a technician proxy and panel-removal space. Use broad painted panels, exposed wear at edges/fasteners and material-specific oil/dust deposits. A hard oblique key reveals stamped/cast shape; avoid uniform black grime. If machinery looks like a riveted cube, add meaningful secondary volumes before bolt scatter. If an access hatch is hidden by a pipe, reroute within the declared subsystem. Deliver panel/structure exploded view and clean/used variants, noting all fictional mechanism assumptions.

branchWorkflows.name: Atompunk
branchWorkflows.procedure: Select a particular retrofuture reference set: rounded enclosures, analog controls, exposed/chrome trim or monumental energy motifs are options, not mandatory historical facts. Build one domestic/public appliance and one infrastructure module sharing radii, control hierarchy and connector vocabulary. Keep operator reach, screen visibility and removable back panel explicit; ornamental atomic rings need clearance from actual handles. Use enamel-like colored coating, limited chrome and readable dials instead of uniform mirror metal. Test warm interior and neutral studio views; large white highlights must not erase control markings. If the design reads only as pastel color, reinforce enclosure/profile and analog interface shape. Deliver front/back/service views and inactive/active displays. Treat period inspiration as a designed interpretation unless independently sourced.

branchWorkflows.name: Solarpunk
branchWorkflows.procedure: Integrate power generation, water, shade, planting and maintenance rather than placing vines on a generic tower. Build a small civic module with solar/shade canopy, drainage/cistern, growing substrate and a repair path. Orient panels and plant zones according to the authored sun/site assumptions; leave service access around connectors and pruning areas. Show seasonal or maintained/overgrown variants when requested. Use warm daylight, varied matte construction and limited reflective panel surfaces. Keep plant root volumes and watering routes visible in cutaway. Plants obscuring panels/doors need relocation or a documented functional tradeoff. If every surface is green, restore material hierarchy and inhabited wear. Deliver water/power/planting layers and maintained-state images; render plausibility does not prove energy output, irrigation performance or sustainability.

branchWorkflows.name: Biopunk
branchWorkflows.procedure: Define whether the system is grown tissue, synthetic imitation or a hybrid. Model containment, nutrient/fluid interface, organic support and technician separation. A wet-lab module needs vessels with actual thickness, ports/tubes ending in appropriate couplings and access for replacement. A grown machine needs branching/attachment logic and inactive/dormant state, not random flesh noise over hard-surface geometry. Separate dry enclosure, translucent membrane, wet tissue and fluid response. Controlled subsurface scale and a backlit diagnostic reveal thickness; avoid using emissive red to conceal missing form. If tubes appear fused without connection or tissue floats, repair interfaces. If subsurface washes out all detail, check units and scale first. Deliver containment/organic layers, exposed/sealed variants and explicit fictional biology; no medical, containment or laboratory safety claim.

branchWorkflows.name: Clockpunk

A gear engraved as relief is different from a moving gear and should be labeled. Use limited brass/steel/wood choices, contact polish and cavity oil. An orthographic exploded view plus side section must reveal clearance between wheels/shafts/frame. If animated teeth intersect, correct ratio, phase, size or pivots before blurring motion. Deliver static/decorative versus animated membership and pivot/ratio sheet; coordinated rotations alone do not prove mechanically valid tooth profiles or efficiency.
